// Every string here is an ordinary word that happens to be a Material Symbols name.
// None of them sits in an icon position, so the codemod must leave the file exactly as it is.
import { useState } from "react"

type Action = "add" | "close" | "search" | "delete" | "edit"
type Level = "info" | "warning" | "error"

export function Panel({ action, level }: { action: Action; level: Level }) {
  const [mode, setMode] = useState<"list" | "search">("list")
  const title = action === "add" ? "Add" : action === "close" ? "Close" : "Search"
  const tone = level === "error" ? "destructive" : level === "warning" ? "attention" : "muted"
  const handlers: Record<Action, () => void> = {
    add: () => setMode("list"),
    close: () => setMode("list"),
    search: () => setMode("search"),
    delete: () => console.error("delete", "warning"),
    edit: () => console.info("edit"),
  }
  switch (action) {
    case "add":
    case "close":
      handlers[action]()
      break
    default:
      handlers["search"]()
  }
  return (
    <form role="search" method="post" data-state={mode} data-level={level} className={tone}>
      <label htmlFor="search">Search, add, close, delete: it's "home" for every list</label>
      <input id="search" type="search" name="search" enterKeyHint="search" autoComplete="email" />
      <input type="password" name="password" />
      <button type="submit" value="send" title={title} aria-label="send">
        {mode === "search" ? "search" : "list"}
      </button>
      <a href="#home" rel="help" target="link">
        {`Press ${"add"} then ${mode}`}
      </a>
      <Tabs defaultValue="inbox" variant="link" orientation="horizontal">
        <Tab value="inbox" name="mail" kind="star" />
      </Tabs>
    </form>
  )
}
export const routes = ["home", "search", "settings", "history"].map((route) => `/${route}`)
export const copy = { close: "Close", search: "Search", label: "label", icon_label: "search" }
export const pattern = /['"](add|close)['"]/
